title: Which evidence drives a network contrast changes across the plausible range of heterogeneity
question: Are the contribution shares that attribute a network meta-analysis contrast to its studies and comparisons stable over the plausible range of the between-study variance, or does conditioning on its point estimate change which evidence appears to drive the result?
design: Three-treatment star and loop networks of 4, 8 or 16 two-arm studies with equal or 5:1 within-study variances and true tau 0, 0.1 or 0.25; hat-matrix contribution shares at tau-hat, over its profile-likelihood interval and at the true tau. 36 cells, 1000 networks each.
answer: No. In a four-study loop network with 5:1 within-study variances, the leading contributing comparison changed across the profile-likelihood interval for tau in 38% to 42% of networks, and the largest single study share moved by about 0.15 on average; with equal within-study variances shares did not move at all. REML put tau at zero in 30% to 67% of four-study networks. The instability comes from the data's inability to distinguish values of tau, not from bias in its estimate.
findings: Leading study changed across the tau interval in 38% to 42% (loop, 4 studies), 27% to 31% (8), 6% to 13% (16).
Shares at tau-hat differed from shares at the true tau by 0.01 to 0.05 on average.
In the star network comparison-level shares are fixed at 50% by construction; study-level leadership changed in 15% to 18% of eight- and sixteen-study networks.
not_answered: One contribution measure (absolute hat-matrix row), three treatments, two-arm studies, frequentist only. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Contribution shares of studies and comparisons to the C versus B contrast
methods_compared: range of shares over the tau profile interval
